policy_title: Invest £6 Billion in Energy Efficiency and Voucher Scheme
stated: The Conservative Party will invest £6 billion in energy efficiency over the next three years to make around a million homes warmer and will fund an energy efficiency voucher scheme, open to all households, to support installations like solar panels.

source.quote: We will invest £6 billion in energy efficiency over the next three years to make around a million homes warmer. And we will fund an energy efficiency voucher scheme, open to every household in England, to support the installation of energy efficiency measures and solar panels, helping families lower their bills.

bearing_set.reason: Direct investment in home energy efficiency and vouchers reduces household energy bills, materially affecting cost of living for ordinary households.
Solar panel installations and energy efficiency upgrades reduce household emissions and support decarbonisation, bearing on the clean environment fundamental.

A voucher scheme 'open to all households' for solar panels is likely regressive in practice — homeowners and higher-income households are better placed to access and use such vouchers, while renters and lower-income households are systematically less able to benefit, risking a widening distributional gap in who captures the subsidy.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: O2 (energy bills are an essential cost), O6 (emissions and climate via efficiency and solar), and O14 (distributional incidence of a universal voucher likely favouring higher-income homeowners). Public-finance effects are not included as the policy text does not specify whether this is funded or borrowed, and absent that information a concrete O12 mechanism cannot be pinned.
